content: Neuroblastoma is the most common extracranial solid tumor in children and represents the most frequent cancer diagnosed during infancy. Its prevalence in the United States is approximately 9 cases per 1,000,000 individuals. The incidence of neuroblastoma decreases with increasing age, with the highest occurrence observed during the first year of life. For individuals aged 25 to 29 years, the incidence is significantly lower, at approximately 3 cases per 1,000,000 individuals. Males are slightly more frequently affected by neuroblastoma compared to females, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 1.2:1. In the United States, the incidence in males is about 6 cases per 1,000,000 individuals, while in females, it is approximately 1 case per 1,000,000 individuals. Neuroblastoma predominantly affects individuals of Caucasian descent. In contrast, individuals of African American, Native Indian, and Asian descent are less likely to develop this malignancy. The incidence among these groups is approximately 1 case per 1,000,000 individuals for African Americans and Native Indians, and 0.8 cases per 1,000,000 individuals for Asians.
